cards.explanation: The reason for the new song is that He has done wonders, friends. The psalm says, "Sing to the LORD a new song, for He has done wonders…" (Psalm 98:1). The new song isn't there to fill a gap in the schedule. It's the answer to what He has done.
The answer is False. The psalm says, "His right hand and holy arm have gained Him the victory." (Psalm 98:1). There's no army in that verse at all, friends. The credit goes to Him and nobody else.

The answer is True. The psalm says, "The LORD has proclaimed His salvation and revealed His righteousness to the nations." (Psalm 98:2). He didn't keep it quiet, friends. The nations are the ones who got to see it.

The psalm is calling on all the earth, friends. It says, "Make a joyful noise to the LORD, all the earth…" (Psalm 98:4). That's the guest list, and it's an invitation that doesn't leave anybody out. That means you, and it means me, even with my singing.
The answer is loud, friends. The psalm says, "break forth—let your cry ring out, and sing praises!" (Psalm 98:4). That's not a whisper. It's a cry that rings out.

The trumpets and the ram's horn join in next, friends. The psalm says, "With trumpets and the blast of the ram’s horn shout for joy before the LORD, the King." (Psalm 98:6). The lyre and harp come first in verse 5. Then the trumpets and the ram's horn join in.

The answer is True. The psalm says, "Let the sea resound, and all that fills it, the world, and all who dwell in it." (Psalm 98:7). The sea gets an invitation, friends, and so does everything in it. The whole world is in the choir.

The reason is that He comes to judge the earth, friends. The rivers clap their hands and the mountains sing together for joy "…before the LORD, for He comes to judge the earth." (Psalm 98:8 and 9). Their joy is tied to His coming.

The word is fair, friends. The psalm says, "He will judge the world with righteousness and the peoples with equity." (Psalm 98:9). Equity means fairness, no thumb on the scale. No wonder creation is singing about it.
